CV Writing & Career Documents

The 6 Essential Components, ATS Optimization & CV vs. Resume Distinction

Academic Lead:Mrs. Ishara Raviharee Weerasinghe(Senior Lecturer in English | Lecturer In Charge)
SLIIT City Uni • Professional Skills Assessment Standard
Curriculum Overview & Context

Details the structural anatomy of an ATS-compliant modern CV. Contrasts Chronological, Functional, and Combination formats, and establishes the definitive boundaries between a CV and a Resume.

Core Competencies & Learning Objectives

  • →Identify the 6 essential anatomical sections of a winning curriculum vitae.
  • →Select appropriately between Chronological, Functional, and Hybrid CV formats.
  • →Optimize career documents to achieve 90%+ parse rates through Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS).
  • →Distinguish between an academic/global CV and a targeted private-sector Resume.
  • →Employ powerful action verbs and quantifiable metrics to validate technical achievements.

The 6 Essential Anatomy Components of a Winning CV

Systematic Engineering of Career Data

Recruiters spend an average of six to seven seconds on an initial CV scan. A winning document must feature an immediate visual hierarchy that guides the human eye directly to relevant competencies and quantifiable value.

1. Header & Verified Contact Data:Full legal name in prominent display, verified professional email (e.g. first.last@domain.com, no casual handles), phone number, location, and verified links to LinkedIn and GitHub.
2. Tailored Professional Summary:High-impact 3-line elevator pitch synthesizing domain specialty, key technologies, and concrete value proposition. Eliminates outdated, self-serving 'Objective' statements.
3. Work & Project Experience:Reverse chronological order, dynamic action verbs ('Architected', 'Refactored', 'Optimized'), and metrics-driven bullet points (e.g. 'Reduced query latency by 38%').
4. Education & Academic Honors:Degree title, university, graduation year (or expected date), GPA/class honors, and specialized relevant coursework.
5. Categorized Skills Inventory:Systematically segregated into Languages, Frameworks, Developer Tools, Databases, and Interpersonal proficiencies.
6. Verified Referees:Two professional or academic contacts with verified corporate titles, official institutional email addresses, and confirmed prior consent.

CV Format Comparative Matrix

Selecting the Right Layout for Your Career Stage

Different career narratives require different architectural containers. Using the wrong format can emphasize employment gaps or conceal critical technical skills.

Format ArchetypeCore Structural FocusIdeal Candidate ProfileATS Friendliness
Chronological CVReverse time progression; emphasizes employer names and tenure length.Candidates with steady, continuous progression in the same industry.Extremely High (Standard industry parser default).
Functional (Skills-Based)Groups accomplishments by skill competencies rather than dates.Career switchers or candidates with significant gaps in employment.Moderate (Can confuse chronological parser algorithms).
Combination / HybridBlends a prominent skill competency matrix with chronological work history.Modern tech undergraduates, full-stack engineers, versatile specialists.High (When styled with clean semantic headers).

ATS Optimization & The CV vs. Resume Distinction

Navigating Algorithmic Gatekeepers

Over 75% of job applications are filtered out by Applicant Tracking Systems before a human recruiter ever sees them.

ATS engines struggle with multi-column table layouts, text placed inside graphical images, complex icons, and non-standard header names.

CV (Curriculum Vitae):Comprehensive, multi-page (2-5+ pages) academic and professional ledger documenting full career history, publications, research, teaching, and credentials. Standard in academia and medicine.
Resume:Highly concise, strictly 1-2 page tailored marketing document custom-built for a specific private-sector vacancy, highlighting only relevant achievements.
Golden Rules for ATS Parsing
“Use standard fonts (Inter, Arial, Calibri), eliminate text boxes and graphics, use universal section titles ('Work Experience', 'Skills', 'Education'), and match exact keywords from the target job specification.”
— Innes (2016)
Recruitment Engineering • ATS Parser Standards

ATS Optimization & CV Format Comparison

The Recommended Architecture for IT Undergraduates

Combination / Hybrid CV Architecture

Blends a prominent categorized technical competencies matrix at the top with a reverse-chronological project and employment ledger below. Allows ATS scanners to ingest exact keywords while human evaluators verify real code repositories and achievements.

ATS Compliance: What to Include
  • • Standard section headings: 'Work Experience', 'Education', 'Skills'.
  • • Universal web-safe typography: Inter, Arial, Calibri, Space Grotesk.
  • • Direct keyword alignment matching the target employer's job description.
  • • Metrics-driven bullet points using verified dynamic action verbs.
ATS Rejection Triggers: What to Avoid
  • • Multi-column nested graphical tables that confuse vertical line parsers.
  • • Important contact or skill text embedded inside raster images or SVG icons.
  • • Outdated 90s 'Objective' statements instead of tailored 3-line pitches.
  • • Unconventional creative titles like 'Full-Stack Ninja' or 'Code Guru'.

Connecting Theory to Practice: Undergraduate & Developer

Reflective analysis connecting CV Writing & Career Documents to coursework at SLIIT City Uni, software engineering projects (LA'CEDRA, TechMart, ApPoint), digital systems at LA'CEDRA, and collaborative teamwork.

01. Meaning & Conceptual Core

A curriculum vitae (CV) is a comprehensive, strategically engineered marketing document designed to present an individual's academic trajectory, technical competencies, verifiable project outcomes, and professional character. It must be optimized simultaneously for automated Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) and the rapid 6-to-10 second cognitive scan of human technical recruiters.

02. Key Theoretical Concepts Acquired
→The 6 Essential Anatomy Components: Contact Header, Professional Summary, Experience/Projects, Education, Categorized Skills, and Referees.
→CV Format Typology: Chronological (continuous progression), Functional (skills-based for transitions), and Combination/Hybrid (the modern gold standard).
→ATS Parsing Architecture: Standard system fonts, avoidance of unparseable graphic columns or text boxes, standard section titles, and job-description keyword matching.
→Action Verb & Metric Formula: Leading every bullet point with dynamic verbs ('Architected', 'Engineered', 'Provisioned', 'Deployed') linked to quantifiable results.
→CV vs. Resume Distinction: Comprehensive multi-page academic/professional record vs. highly condensed 1–2 page private-sector marketing document.
IT//EQ
03. Industry Imperative — Why This Matters in Tech

The global tech industry relies heavily on automated ATS filters to screen thousands of resumes. A developer with exceptional full-stack skills will be automatically discarded before reaching an engineering manager if their document utilizes non-standard fonts, unparseable tables, or lacks relevant technical keywords. Precision formatting is a non-negotiable entry barrier.

08. Personal Key Takeaways

01.Format for the ATS parser; write for the human engineering hiring manager.
02.Every bullet point must pair an active power verb with a technical context and a verifiable positive outcome.

Core Academic Takeaways

01.

A winning CV contains 6 core components; the professional summary must be a 3-line value pitch, not an outdated objective.

02.

The Hybrid/Combination format is the gold standard for tech students, combining technical skill clusters with reverse-chronological evidence.

03.

ATS algorithms filter out over 75% of CVs; optimize with standard headings, single-column parsing, and job-specific keywords.

04.

A CV is an exhaustive academic and professional chronicle; a Resume is a 1-2 page tailored marketing brochure.

Academic Literature & Primary Citations (APA 7th)

Reflective Learning Prompt & Target Action

“Analyze your current CV: how many bullet points begin with passive duties rather than dynamic action verbs with quantifiable metrics?”

Target Action:Rewrite at least four bullet points using the formula: [Action Verb] + [Technical Tool/Task] + [Quantified Result/Impact].

Assessment Viva Voce Protocol (Random Question Box)

4 Questions
Randomized Assessment Questions:
  • Q01.Explain three architectural reasons why an ATS algorithm might reject an otherwise qualified developer's CV.
  • Q02.Differentiate between a Curriculum Vitae and a Resume in purpose, length, and industry context.
  • Q03.What are the six mandatory anatomy sections of a winning CV?
  • Q04.Rewrite a weak bullet point ('Responsible for fixing bugs') into a high-impact, metrics-driven statement.
Defense Protocol & Conduct:
  • Bring two printed physical copies of your hybrid CV in pristine portfolio folders.
  • Be prepared to verbally defend any single bullet point or technology listed in your skills inventory.
  • Explain the strategic reasoning behind your chosen CV format.
